summary: Root cause: the cost-optimisation config change cfg-2207, which shrank portfolio-service db.pool.max_size from 50 to 5 at 2026-03-10T09:52:00Z, is insufficient for the pre-existing steady demand of ~12 concurrent DB connections (~2.4x the new cap). Within ~79s the pool pinned at exactly 5/5/0 in-use with 25-57 requests waiting on the 3000ms acquire timeout, portfolio-service p99 stepped >20x, and api-gateway's upstream calls surfaced as 504s on /v1/portfolio/*. Confidence 0.86 (high). The reporter's suspicion of the api-gateway HTTP/2 deploy (dep-5220) is refuted by timing (08:00Z, ~1h53m before onset with no intervening portfolio-path change) and by an error signature that is purely local pool-wait, not stream/connection failure; ledger-db and redis-cache were healthy and their connection counts actually fell. Remediation is to revert cfg-2207 to 50 (or re-apply a right-sized profile).

ranked_hypotheses.title: portfolio-service JDBC pool shrunk to 5 (cfg-2207) is insufficient for steady pre-existing demand, saturating the pool and cascading to gateway 504s
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A cost-optimisation config change (cfg-2207) reduced portfolio-service db.pool.max_size from 50 to 5 at 09:52:00Z. Pre-change pool demand was already ~12-13 concurrent connections (2.4x the new cap) at unchanged request rate; within ~60-80s the pool pinned at exactly 5/5/0 in-use, requests blocked on the 3000ms acquire timeout, portfolio-service latency stepped >20x, and api-gateway's upstream calls to portfolio-service timed out as 504s. The fault originates in the config change, not in the gateway or the DB.

causal_chain.claim: cfg-2207 sets portfolio-service db.pool.max_size 50 -> 5 at 09:52:00Z (infra-automation, 'cost-optimisation profile small'; old_value=50 recorded explicitly) [F2,F14,F26]
Pre-change concurrent DB demand was already ~11.9-13.3, i.e. ~2.4x the new cap of 5, so 5 connections is materially insufficient rather than removal of harmless over-provisioning [F19,F20]
Demand was flat across onset (request_rate 526-596 req/s every minute 09:30-10:10Z), so the saturation is capacity-driven, not load-driven [F23]

Pool pins at its new cap immediately: db_pool_in_use steps from avg 11.89 at 09:52Z to exactly 5.0 (max 5, zero variation) at 09:53Z and stays pinned through 10:10Z — the signature of a cap being hit, not a transient [F21]

Requests then block >3000ms and fail: 'could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms' (270) and HikariPool-1 'Connection is not available, request timed out after 3000ms (total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=25-57)' (233); no network/dead-connection text, i.e. local pool exhaustion, not hung upstream calls [F9,F10,F34]

portfolio-service p99 jumps in the first bucket after the change: flat 172-191ms through the 09:52Z bucket, 4250.91ms at 09:53Z (600s buckets: ~180ms -> 3031/4546ms, then ~4.0-4.3s through 11:50Z) [F8,F22]

api-gateway's upstream call to portfolio-service exceeds its timeout: logs 'upstream timeout portfolio-service GET /v<n>/portfolio/holdings' and 504s for GET /v1/portfolio/holdings from 09:53:53Z (252-256 occurrences, dominant gateway WARN) [F7,F12]

Ordering: cfg-2207 (09:52Z) precedes the first Hikari/JDBC error (09:53:19Z, ~79s) and first gateway 504 (09:53:53Z, ~113s); it is the temporally last change on the portfolio path before onset, was never reverted (no revert record; only config change in the store for all services 09:52-11:59Z), so the live size at 11:59Z matches the observed total=5 [F15,F16,F28,F29,F30]

Same change class as precedent HIST-115 (order-service): 'Datasource pool size overridden by a wrong environment profile' -> 'connection is not available', 'pool exhausted', fixed by reverting config [F6,F17]

assumptions: The write to db.pool.max_size was actually pushed to and loaded by the running instances at 09:52Z — the config record has no apply/effective timestamp or rollout-status field (F27), and the effective live pool size before/after is inferred from old_value=50 + the runtime total=5, not from a direct live-pool gauge

The 5 held connections are being consumed by healthy-but-numerous requests rather than held indefinitely by slow backend calls (partially mitigated by F34's absence of network/dead-connection errors and F31/F32's healthy ledger-db, but not directly proven since waiting/acquire-time are only in logs, not a time series)

ranked_hypotheses.title: api-gateway v9.3.0 (dep-5220) HTTP/2-to-upstream rewrite causes slow/blocked upstream calls and 504s (reporter's suspicion)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The api-gateway envoy 1.29->1.30 upgrade with HTTP/2 enabled to upstreams (dep-5220, 08:00Z) introduced faulty multiplexing/stream handling toward portfolio-service, so gateway-originated calls stall and surface as upstream timeouts and 504s, possibly via a ~2h delayed effect on upstream connection usage.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5220 deploys api-gateway v9.3.0 at 08:00:00Z: envoy 1.29->1.30, upstream protocol h2 for portfolio-service and order-service; still live, rolled_back_at null [F1,F13]
The envoy/HTTP-2 change alters upstream connection and stream behavior toward portfolio-service [ASSUMED — no per-route/per-connection data, no gateway stream-pool metrics]
Gateway-to-portfolio-service calls stall or over-subscribe connections, producing upstream timeouts and 504s [ASSUMED]

The same mechanism would have to drive portfolio-service's Hikari pool exhaustion at total=5 — but that pool is capped at 5 (cfg-2207) and the acquire errors are pure Hikari pool-wait, not upstream/stream failures [F9,F34]
Historic precedent HIST-116 is the same class (envoy upgrade changed HTTP/2 max concurrent streams -> 504s at gateway, upstream resets, resolved by rollback) [F5,F17]

assumptions: The HTTP/2 enablement has a ~1h53m delayed effect on portfolio-service's DB connection usage (no echo of dep-5220 anywhere in the portfolio path)
The gateway failure mechanism is stream/connection over-subscription from the envoy change rather than anything downstream
dep-5220 was not rolled back and the incident persisted regardless (consistent with F13, but no recovery test exists)

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared ledger-db degraded (failover/saturation), holding portfolio-service pool connections and cascading to gateway 504s
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The shared ledger-db on the portfolio path degraded (slow queries, failover, or its own limits), so portfolio-service's pool connections hung on DB calls, new acquires timed out, and latency propagated to gateway 504s. Precedent HIST-102 (portfolio timeouts/504s from a ledger-db primary failover) matches this class. This is now heavily contradicted by ledger-db metrics.

causal_chain.claim: Portfolio path is api-gateway -> portfolio-service -> {ledger-db (shared), market-data-service, redis-cache (shared)}; ledger-db also serves order-service and payment-service [F3,F18]

ledger-db becomes slow/unavailable (failover, saturation, held connections) near onset [ASSUMED — contradicted: cpu 26-32%, connections_active FELL 61.8->50.9, slow_queries 0.2-1.58 no spike, replication_lag flat ~40ms across 09:30-10:10Z] [F31,F32]

portfolio-service DB operations block, holding pool connections so new acquires time out after 3000ms [contradicted: errors are pure Hikari pool-wait at total=5 with no 'connection is dead'/'communications link failure'/socket text, i.e. connections were not blocked on an unreachable upstream] [F9,F34]
portfolio-service p99 steps >20x and gateway upstream calls time out as 504s [F8,F7,F12]
Historic precedent HIST-102: portfolio page timeouts / 504 at gateway caused by ledger-db primary failover [F18]

assumptions: ledger-db had a fault or saturation on 2026-03-10 (no failover/restart event endpoint was queried; absence of failover is inferred from flat replication lag and falling connection counts)
A backend fault began near 09:52Z despite flat 09:50-10:10Z metrics

ranked_hypotheses.title: Traffic/load growth exhausted a right-sized portfolio-service pool with no single triggering change (capacity saturation)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Portfolio request volume grew past what the provisioned DB connections could serve, and the pool exhausted organically; the gateway 504s are the downstream symptom and the cfg-2207 timing is coincidental.

causal_chain.claim: portfolio-service DB connection demand increases with traffic [CONTRADICTED: request_rate held 526.33-595.78 req/s every minute 09:30-10:10Z, including 585.08 at 09:52 and 549.27 at 09:53 — no traffic surge at onset] [F23]
Provisioned pool capacity is insufficient and the pool saturates (total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=25-57) [F9]
Requests time out on acquisition, lifting portfolio-service latency and cascading to gateway 504s [F8,F7]

assumptions: Traffic or per-request DB concurrency grew materially around 09:50Z with no accompanying change

facts.statement: A single config change on the portfolio path, cfg-2207, reduced portfolio-service db.pool.max_size from an explicit old_value=50 to new_value=5 at 2026-03-10T09:52:00Z, authored by infra-automation under the 'cost-optimisation profile small' description; it is the only config change returned for portfolio-service today.

Pre-change concurrent DB demand was ~11.5-13.3 connections (mean ~12.0) and was steady across 06:00-09:52Z, i.e. roughly 2.4x the new cap of 5 — 5 connections is materially insufficient, not removal of harmless over-provisioning.

Pool saturation begins exactly at the cfg-2207 effective time: db_pool_in_use steps from avg 11.89 at 09:52:00Z to a pinned avg=5.0/max=5 from 09:53:00Z onward and stays exactly at 5.0 through 10:10:00Z with zero variation.

portfolio-service latency stepped >20x, from flat ~180ms (172.69-191.43ms at 60s resolution) through the 09:52:00Z bucket to 4250.91ms at 09:53:00Z (max 4546.30ms at 09:54), and stayed elevated ~4050-4260ms avg through 11:50Z.

portfolio-service errors are pure Hikari pool-wait timeouts, not network/connection failures: 'could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms' (earliest 09:53:19Z) and 'HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available, request timed out after 3000ms (total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=25..57)', 503 ERROR entries in 06:00-11:59Z with no 'connection is dead'/'socket read'/'communications link failure' text.

api-gateway began logging 504s for GET /v1/portfolio/holdings at 2026-03-10T09:53:53Z, with the dominant gateway WARN being 'upstream timeout portfolio-service GET /v<n>/portfolio/holdings' (252 occurrences); the gateway error is an upstream timeout whose latency originates downstream in portfolio-service.

Demand was flat across onset — request_rate held 526.33-595.78 req/s every minute from 09:30 to 10:10Z — and CPU was not saturated (cpu_pct 33.99-38.52%, mean 35.84%), so neither a traffic surge nor compute explains the latency step.

The shared backends on the portfolio path were healthy and did not precede onset: ledger-db cpu_pct 26.26-32.15%, slow_queries_per_min 0.2-1.58 with no spike, replication_lag_ms flat 36.26-42.77, and connections_active FELL from ~61.83 at 09:50Z to 50.92 (min 49.31) at 09:54Z; redis-cache cpu_pct 20.14-23.73% and memory_pct 64.43-77.01% with no step at 09:50-09:53Z.

cfg-2207 at 09:52:00Z precedes the first portfolio-service Hikari/JDBC error (09:53:19Z) by ~79s and the first gateway 504 (09:53:53Z) by ~113s, and is the last change on the portfolio path before onset; there is no deployment or config change to the portfolio path between 08:00Z and 09:52Z.

The only code/config deployment on 2026-03-10 was dep-5220, api-gateway v9.3.0 at 08:00:00Z ('envoy 1.29->1.30; upstream protocol h2 for portfolio-service and order-service'), status 'live' with rolled_back_at null — ~1h53m before onset, and there is no portfolio-service code deployment in the window (it changed only via config).

cfg-2207 was not reverted within the data window: no revert record exists in the config-change store, no deployment or rollout-revert record exists for portfolio-service or api-gateway after onset, so the effective live size at 11:59Z is consistent with new_value=5, matching the saturated runtime pool total=5.

portfolio-service exposes no db_pool_idle/db_pool_waiting/db_pool_acquire_time or concurrent-requests metric — only db_pool_in_use is available — so the waiting=25-57 queue depth and acquire-timeout behaviour come from Hikari log lines rather than a time series.

The cfg-2207 change record exposes only id, service, key, old_value, new_value, changed_at, author, description — no apply/effective timestamp, target revision, or apply-failure/partial-rollout field — so 'written vs applied to live instances' cannot be distinguished from the record itself.

assumptions: The write to db.pool.max_size was actually pushed to and loaded by the running portfolio-service instances at 09:52Z; the config record has no apply/effective timestamp or rollout-status field (F27), so the effective live pool size before/after is inferred from old_value=50 plus the runtime total=5, not from a direct live-pool gauge.

The 5 held connections are consumed by healthy-but-numerous requests rather than held indefinitely by slow backend calls; this is supported by the absence of network/dead-connection errors (F34) and by healthy ledger-db/redis-cache (F31-F33), but waiting/acquire-time exist only in logs, not as a time series (F25).

The specific DB the 5 pooled connections pointed at is not literally named in the log text; identification relies on the known dependency mapping portfolio-service -> ledger-db plus the absence of network-failure stack text.

No failover/restart event endpoint was queried for ledger-db, so the absence of a failover at 09:50-09:55Z is inferred from flat replication lag and falling connection counts rather than from an explicit 'no event' record (F31/F32).

(demoted from facts: no verified observation backs it) Precedent class match: HIST-115 (2025-09-25, order-service) had symptoms 'connection is not available','request timed out','pool exhausted' with root cause 'Datasource pool size overridden by a wrong environment profile' and resolution 'Reverted config' — the same change class as cfg-2207.

timeline.event: Only deployment of the day: dep-5220, api-gateway v9.3.0 (envoy 1.29->1.30, HTTP/2 to upstreams); status live, never rolled back.
Steady-state demand on portfolio-service DB pool: db_pool_in_use ~11.5-13.3 concurrent connections (mean ~12.0), ~2.4x the eventual new cap of 5.
portfolio-service p99 latency still flat at ~180ms; ledger-db and redis-cache metrics healthy and flat; ledger-db connections_active at ~61.83 avg.

cfg-2207 applied: portfolio-service db.pool.max_size 50 -> 5 by infra-automation ('cost-optimisation profile small'). Last change on the portfolio path; no intervening change since the 08:00Z gateway deploy.
Pool pins at exactly total=5/active=5/idle=0 (avg 5.0, zero variation onward); latency jumps to 4250.91ms in the first 60s bucket after the config change.
First portfolio-service ERROR: 'could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms'; Hikari reports pool exhausted with waiting=25..57; ledger-db connections_active falling (56.44 avg).
First api-gateway 504 logged for GET /v1/portfolio/holdings, qualified as an upstream timeout to portfolio-service (252 occurrences of that pattern).
latency_p99_ms peaks at 4546.30ms; cpu_pct flat at 35.88% (no compute saturation); ledger-db slow_queries and redis-cache metrics unchanged.
portfolio-service latency still elevated ~4050-4260ms avg; pool remains pinned at 5.0 through 10:10Z with no recovery and no cfg-2207 revert record.

recommended_actions.action: Revert cfg-2207: restore portfolio-service db.pool.max_size to 50 (or re-apply a right-sized profile with max_size >= 15, above the observed ~12-13 concurrent demand) via infra-automation, then confirm the runtime Hikari pool total rises above 5 and that 'could not acquire JDBC connection' errors and gateway 504s stop.
recommended_actions.rationale: cfg-2207 (50 -> 5 at 09:52Z) is the origin; the pool is pinned at total=5/active=5/idle=0 with waiting=25-57 and latency >20x. Since 5 < pre-change demand of ~12-13, only restoring a sufficient cap clears the saturation. Precedent HIST-115 was resolved by reverting the pool-size config.

recommended_actions.action: Do not roll back dep-5220 (gateway v9.3.0 HTTP/2) as the first mitigation; if the gateway planned a rollback, defer it, since reverting the gateway is not indicated by evidence and would add risk during the outage.
recommended_actions.rationale: The deploy at 08:00Z precedes onset by ~1h53m with no intervening portfolio-path change, and the error signature is local Hikari pool-wait (no stream/connection failure text), contradicting H2.

recommended_actions.action: Verify recovery explicitly: after reverting cfg-2207, watch portfolio-service latency_p99_ms return to ~180ms and db_pool_in_use rise off the pinned 5.0 without the pool re-saturating, and confirm gateway 504 WARNs cease within the same window.
recommended_actions.rationale: The pool has stayed pinned at exactly 5.0 with no recovery through the data window because cfg-2207 was never reverted (no revert record exists); recovery confirmation both closes the incident and confirms the causal chain.

recommended_actions.action: Add a config-change safety guard on db.pool.max_size (and comparable datasource keys): block or require approval for reductions below observed peak demand, and add an apply/effective timestamp, target revision, and rollout/apply-failure status field to the config-change record so 'written' vs 'applied to live instances' is unambiguous.
recommended_actions.rationale: cfg-2207 was a cost-optimisation profile applied by automation that cut capacity ~10x below steady demand, and the change record exposes no apply timestamp or rollout status (F27), which is exactly what made the causal link inferential rather than directly provable.

recommended_actions.action: Remove or cap the 'cost-optimisation profile small' datasource sizing rule for request-serving services, or gate it behind a load-based review, so an automated profile cannot shrink a JDBC pool below measured concurrency.
recommended_actions.rationale: cfg-2207 came from infra-automation under 'cost-optimisation profile small' (F2/F14/F26); HIST-115 shows the identical failure class (wrong environment profile overriding datasource pool size). This is a preventable recurrence.

recommended_actions.action: Emit or expose db_pool_idle / db_pool_waiting / db_pool_acquire_time and a live datasource max_size gauge for portfolio-service, and alert on pool saturation and acquire-timeout rate so pool exhaustion is detected as a gauge before it becomes gateway 504s.
recommended_actions.rationale: Only db_pool_in_use exists today (no idle/waiting/acquire-time or live max_size), so queue depth had to be read from log lines and the effective live pool size could not be gauged directly — the key monitoring blind spot in this incident.

recommended_actions.action: Fix gateway-side observability: api-gateway's own latency_p99_ms and resource metrics were unavailable (repeated 503s), so gateway p99 magnitude and local saturation could never be confirmed numerically; restore/repair that metric pipeline.
recommended_actions.rationale: api-gateway latency and cpu/memory/connection-pool metrics failed to query throughout the investigation, leaving the gateway's own contribution unmeasured (only upstream-timeout log evidence was available).

data_gaps: No direct live datasource max_size gauge or instance-level pool-size read was taken; the effective live pool size before/after 09:52Z is supported indirectly (old_value=50 + runtime total=5), not by a gauge for both timestamps.

cfg-2207's record has no apply/effective timestamp, target revision, or apply-failure/partial-rollout field (F27), so whether the write was actually loaded by running instances at 09:52Z rather than merely written/pending cannot be proven from the store.

api-gateway latency_p99_ms and cpu/memory/connection-pool/restart metrics could not be retrieved (repeated 503 backend-unavailable), so the gateway's own p99 magnitude, exact metric onset, and local resource saturation are unconfirmed.

portfolio-service has no db_pool_idle/db_pool_waiting/db_pool_acquire_time or concurrent-requests metric, so waiting queue depth and per-acquire latency around 09:52Z come only from Hikari log lines, not a 60s time series.

No datastore failover/restart/audit event endpoint was queried for ledger-db; the absence of a failover at onset is inferred from flat replication_lag_ms and falling connection counts rather than an explicit no-event record.
ledger-db disk_used_pct and redis-cache hit_ratio_pct queries were never executed (budget exhausted), so disk exhaustion on ledger-db and cache-hit degradation remain unverified as contributors.

A get_config_changes call for all services over 2026-03-09 00:00Z-11:59Z failed with 503, and the 00:00Z-09:00Z portfolio-service bucket was not queried (budget exhausted), so a config change on a shared component (ledger-db, redis-cache, market-data-service) or an earlier portfolio-service change cannot be fully excluded.

The historical-incident search for a 'gateway deploy with delayed pool-exhaustion effect' timed out, so the historic corpus was only partially searched and H2's delayed-effect mechanism is neither confirmed nor refuted from precedent.

No data on whether dep-5220's HTTP/2 enablement is per-route or per-connection toward portfolio-service, nor any gateway-side stream/connection-pool metrics toward portfolio-service, so H2's mechanism cannot be directly tested.
Portfolio-service error log entries carry no JDBC URL, SQL statement or datasource name, so the connection target (ledger-db vs another DB) is not literally named in the logs.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Recovery test: if reverting cfg-2207 to 50 (or right-sizing it) does NOT restore portfolio-service p99 to ~180ms and clear the pool saturation and gateway 504s, H1's causal chain is broken and the origin must be re-examined.

Direct evidence that the db.pool.max_size 50->5 write was never loaded by live instances (e.g. an apply log, a live max_size gauge showing 50 through 09:53Z, or a failed/partial rollout record) would invalidate H1's premise.

A live datasource max_size gauge or instance config dump showing the pool was already 5 (or otherwise capped) before 09:52Z, with saturation preceding the change, would move the origin away from cfg-2207.

Evidence that ledger-db or redis-cache degraded before 09:53:19Z — a failover/restart event, a slow-query or replication-lag spike, or a rising ledger-db connections_active at onset — would revive H3 as the origin.

Gateway-side evidence that dep-5220 introduced stream/connection over-subscription toward portfolio-service at ~09:50Z (gateway 504s preceding portfolio-service latency, h2 stream resets, or upstream connection-pool exhaustion on the gateway with local resource saturation) would revive H2.
A material rise in request rate or per-request DB concurrency starting at ~09:50Z (rather than the observed flat 526-596 req/s) would support H4 capacity saturation over a triggering change.

findings.statement: Dependency mapping: portfolio-service -> ledger-db (db, shared:true), market-data-service (http), redis-cache (cache, shared:true); ledger-db is shared and also reached by order-service and payment-service, and redis-cache is shared by portfolio-service, market-data-service and auth-service. A third precedent HIST-102 (2025-09-02) is portfolio page timeouts / 504 at gateway caused by ledger-db primary failover, so the shared datastore on the critical path is a candidate contribution. No deployment to portfolio-service itself exists in this window, so portfolio-service was changed only via config.

portfolio-service db_pool_in_use was stable at ~11.5-12.7 connections throughout 06:00-09:52Z (60s buckets 09:30-09:52 avg 10.78-12.70; 300s buckets 06:00-09:30 mean 12.01, max 13.3), with no single 60s bucket at or below 10.67 before onset.

Concurrent DB demand exceeded 5 users well before 09:52Z: pre-change in-use values include 12.70, 12.67, 12.63 and 13.3 (300s max), so demand sat at roughly 2.4x the new max_size of 5 — 5 connections is materially insufficient, not harmless over-provisioning of 50.

Pool saturation begins exactly at the cfg-2207 effective time: db_pool_in_use steps from avg 11.89 at 09:52:00Z to avg=5.0/max=5 at 09:53:00Z and stays pinned at exactly 5.0 through 10:10:00Z with zero variation (missing_points 0), i.e. the pool is permanently at its new cap rather than recovering.

Latency onset is co-located with the pool cap at 60s resolution: latency_p99_ms is flat 172.69-191.43ms through the 09:52:00Z bucket, then jumps to 4250.91ms at 09:53:00Z (max 4546.30ms at 09:54) — the first elevated bucket is the one immediately following the 09:52Z config change, not earlier.

Demand was unchanged across the onset: request_rate held 526.33-595.78 req/s every minute from 09:30 to 10:10Z (including 585.08 at 09:52 and 549.27 at 09:53), so the latency step and pool pinning were not driven by a traffic surge.
The service was not CPU-saturated at any point: cpu_pct stayed 33.99-38.52% (mean 35.84%) across 09:30-10:10Z, flat through 09:54 (35.88%) — so the slowdown is pool-wait, not compute.

portfolio-service exposes no db_pool_idle / db_pool_waiting / db_pool_acquire_time or concurrent-requests metric — the only pool metric available is db_pool_in_use (available_metrics: cpu_pct, db_pool_in_use, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, request_rate, restarts), so idle/waiting/acquire-time at 60s must come from the Hikari log lines rather than a time series.

The only config-application record for portfolio-service is cfg-2207: db.pool.max_size old_value=50 -> new_value=5, changed_at 2026-03-10T09:52:00Z, author infra-automation, description 'Apply cost-optimisation profile 'small' to service datasource'. The explicit old_value=50 is the recorded pre-change (running) size and new_value=5 the post-change size.

The config-change record for cfg-2207 exposes no separate apply/effective timestamp, no target revision, and no apply-failure or partial-rollout field — the returned object contains only id, service, key, old_value, new_value, changed_at, author, description. So 'applied vs merely written' cannot be distinguished, and no apply-failure/partial-rollout record exists in this shape.

No deployment of any kind exists for portfolio-service in 09:00Z-11:59Z or 09:52Z-2026-03-11T23:59Z (count 0 both), and none for api-gateway in 09:50Z-11:59Z; therefore there is no rollout-revert or follow-up deployment record that could represent a cfg-2207 revert.

Across ALL services for 2026-03-10T09:52:00Z-11:59:59Z the only config change returned is cfg-2207 itself (count 1); likewise portfolio-service 09:00Z-2026-03-11T23:59Z returns only cfg-2207 (count 1). No second cfg entry for db.pool.max_size and no other service's change appears, i.e. no revert record for cfg-2207 exists in the config-change store for the reviewed window.

cfg-2207 (09:52:00Z) is temporally the last change on the portfolio path before onset (09:53:19Z Hikari/JDBC errors, 09:53:53Z gateway 504s) and was not reverted within the data window, so the effective live size at 11:59Z is consistent with new_value=5 — matching the saturated pool total=5 observed by the observability agent; the config change remained in force (no rolled-back/reverted flag anywhere in the records).

ledger-db was healthy across 09:30-10:10Z: cpu_pct stayed 26.26-32.15% (mean 30.03), connections_active 49.31-66.03 (mean 58.43, in fact DROPPING from ~61 at 09:50 to 50.92 avg at 09:54), slow_queries_per_min 0.2-1.58 (mean 1.06, no spike; 09:50 avg 0.63 and 09:54 avg 1.09), replication_lag_ms 36.26-42.77 (mean 39.86, flat) — no saturation, no query slowdown, no failover signature at 09:50-09:55Z.

ledger-db active connections FELL during onset rather than rising: 61.83 avg at 09:50Z -> 56.44 at 09:52Z -> 50.92 (min 49.31) at 09:54Z, then ~54-56 through 10:10Z. A backend under load/starving clients would show the opposite, so the DB did not become the bottleneck; portfolio-service's shrinking client pool (5) is the more likely reason its connections dropped.

redis-cache was healthy across 09:30-10:10Z: cpu_pct 20.14-23.73% (mean 22.05, no step at 09:50-09:53) and memory_pct 64.43-77.01% (mean 70.27, no growth trend). No cache-side saturation coincident with onset.

The portfolio-service JDBC errors are pure Hikari pool-wait timeouts, not network/connection failures: both patterns are 'could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms' and 'HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available, request timed out after 3000ms (total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=25..57)'. There is no 'connection is dead', 'socket read', 'communications link failure' or SQLException/COMMS-link text, i.e. the held connections were NOT blocked on an unreachable upstream — the pool was locally exhausted at total=5.

refs.quote: HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available, request timed out after 3000ms (total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=43)
GET /v1/portfolio/holdings failed: could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms

findings.statement: TIMELINE for H3: backend (ledger-db, redis-cache) degradation does NOT precede portfolio-service's 09:53:19Z acquire timeouts. ledger-db and redis-cache metrics are flat across 09:50-09:55Z with no failover/restart/lag/CPU/slow-query signature, while portfolio-service's first JDBC timeout is at 09:53:19Z. Backend datastore health therefore does not explain the onset.
